proposal: The Mandate recommends reassessing all US aid programs in Latin America and ending those that have not produced results. USAID would then focus on free-market fundamentals (property rights, a functioning judiciary, labor and pension reform, lower taxes, deregulation), challenge socialist ideas, fund private-sector partnerships and pro-market civil society, and commit to shifting the whole regional portfolio to local organizations by 2030. It notes that the first-term America Crece investment initiative was cancelled.

status_summary: In the successor structure the reassess-and-terminate element happened through the global review rather than a results-based regional one: the Secretary of State announced on 2025-03-10 that about 5,200 of 6,200 USAID programs (about 83 percent) were eliminated (a global figure; no regional breakdown for Latin America was confirmed), and USAID's remaining operations merged into State on 2025-07-01. For the positive agenda, the National Security Strategy released 2025-12-04 calls for commercial diplomacy and for tying aid terms to winding down adversary influence; State's 2026 to 2030 strategic plan was not read, and reported regional aid targets in it remain unverified. Against the text, a U.S. senator stated at a hearing on 2025-09-03 that State's democracy bureau had cancelled 389 of 391 democracy grants (a statement not independently verified), which runs against support for pro-market and democratic civil society, and no 2030 localization commitment, free-market reform program or America Crece successor was found. The stage is in_progress at the low end because the terminations are operative and the regional reorientation is stated in strategy, while the text's positive program elements are not shown.

timeline.event: The Secretary of State announced that the review of USAID programs was complete, with about 5,200 of 6,200 programs (about 83 percent) eliminated worldwide and the rest to be managed under State.
USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department.

At a Senate Foreign Relations Committee nominations hearing, Senator Chris Murphy tells the nominee for Assistant Secretary for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor that 389 of the bureau's 391 democracy promotion grants have been canceled (the senator's statement, per his office's release of that date; not independently verified).

The White House released the National Security Strategy (cover dated November 2025), whose Western Hemisphere section calls for commercial diplomacy, DFC and other financing for US investment, and aid terms contingent on winding down adversary influence.

title: Reassess Latin America aid, end failed programs, back free markets and localize by 2030
uncertainties: Unverified lead, low confidence: the Washington Office on Latin America (an advocacy group) estimates from a March 2025 memo to Congress, which was not read, that more than 84 percent of USAID assistance to Latin America and the Caribbean was cut; no news report or official document with a regional figure was found in three searches. The 83 percent figure is global and computed from AP program counts. The 389 of 391 grant figure is a senator's statement recorded in his office's release, not an agency figure. Unverified lead, low confidence: the State 2026 to 2030 strategic plan was not read (state.gov is blocked from this environment). A Devex Newswire issue of 2026-01-29 (copy hosted by the USAID Alumni Association) reported that it gives the Western Hemisphere and East Asia together about 40 percent of foreign assistance, shifts from grant aid toward trade and private-sector growth and selects partners partly by security ties, migration cooperation and voting alignment, with no dollar amounts; a 2026-01-19 report on harici.com.tr, an outlet of uncertain standing, describes a target of at least 40 percent for the two regions combined. Neither account was confirmed against the plan or a reputable news report, so no event or stage finding rests on them. The National Security Strategy was read directly by the researcher and again in review on 2026-10-18 (cover November 2025; release date 2025-12-04 from Lawfare); its Western Hemisphere section supports commercial diplomacy and aid terms tied to winding down adversary influence and does not use the term localization. The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, enacted 2026-02-03) was confirmed on its govinfo.gov BILLSTATUS record (re-read in review) only; its foreign operations text was not opened, and an advocacy-group (WOLA) account of its democracy and Central America provisions is an unverified lead at low confidence. No revival of America Crece, 2030 localization commitment or pro-market civil society funding line was found. Executive Order 14217 is background only. A CRS search returned only a pre-2025 report (R48266) with no usable figures. Judgment: in_progress 25 kept over diverged or proposed.
